thread:
maria: Quick proposal: change the Python/TS SDK default for route preference handling. Currently SDKs silently rewrite legacy `X-Route` -> `x-route-pref` and enable implicit route fallback. I want to flip the default to strict mode (no implicit rewrite/fallback) in the next minor, warn for one release, and then require an explicit opt-in shim for old behavior when we bump the major.

maria: Motivation: we've been seeing unpredictable quota attributions and console dashboards showing mixed tenants when fallback happens. Strict mode makes routing deterministic and aligns with the console's per-route billing. It does mean some clients will start getting fallback errors if they rely on silent behavior.

jordan: +1 on determinism. important: we need a clear deprecation path in the SDKs so production apps don't break. can we provide both a runtime opt-in and an env var for 1-2 releases?

maria: Yes. Plan:
- next minor (canary first): introduce `strict_route_pref` default = false but log a WARNING when legacy header is detected.
- following minor: change default to true, still log warnings for a single minor.
- major bump (2 months after announcement): remove implicit rewrite; keep a compat flag `ROUTE_PREF_LEGACY_SHIM=true` in env for emergency rollback.

samir: For Go client: there is also an init-order race we hit if we add shim that mutates headers. Need to ensure the shim runs before retries/backoff logic intercepts headers.

kevin: UX on console: we'll add a policy banner and a per-tenant gauge showing % of requests using legacy header in the next console deploy. That helps customers find which services to patch.

maria: Example migration snippet for Python SDK I drafted:

```python
# old behavior (implicit rewrite)
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))

# new explicit shim
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), strict_route_pref=True)
```

maria: And for heavy traffic customers who can't change app code immediately, we'll document the `ROUTE_PREF_LEGACY_SHIM` env fallback: set to `true` on the process or pod to restore previous behavior. Mark it as emergency-only.

jordan: Telemetry: we should emit a distinct telemetry tag for "shim_applied" so billing/console can filter. Also include sampling for the first 1000 requests after deploy to audit surface area.

samir: For TS SDK: any change to default will be a semver-major for a short-lived time? We typically avoid major bumps for these changes; can we make it a minor with opt-out to reduce churn?

maria: We can needle it as a minor at first (default false) but plan the major for final removal. Communication will be explicit: CHANGELOG, Console banner, in-SDK deprecation warning + link to migration guide.

kevin: Docs checklist:
- migration page with code snippets for Python/TS/Go
- console banner text + FAQ
- changelog entry explaining timeline and env var usage
- sample k8s rollout patch for adding env var to pods

maria: Release mechanics:
- stage 1 (canary): release SDK minor that adds warnings and the `strict_route_pref` param. Mark it experimental. Push to canary users (internal + 3 customers).
- stage 2 (observability): add console metric + route-legacy-percent tile to tenant dashboard.
- stage 3 (wider rollout): flip default to true in SDK minor and surface strong WARN logs.
- stage 4 (major): remove shim, major bump if needed, env var remains but documented as escape hatch.

release-bot: deploy canary scheduled: 2025-09-14T16:00Z -> SDK canary pipeline kicked. :rocket:

jordan: Concern: rate-limited customers may rely on fallback for QoS. We should add a fallback policy on the routing plane that translates a missing header into a well-defined low-priority route instead of global fallback; this keeps apps alive but correctly attributes quota to a shared "legacy" bucket. Ops, thoughts?

samir: That sounds reasonable as an interim. We'll need to add a flag to the routing API to enable "legacy-queue" route mapping per tenant. Does that exist?

maria: Not yet. eng-platform - can you add a tenant-level toggle so we can enable legacy-queue only for tenants who request it? That reduces blast radius.

jordan: I'll open a tracking ticket for the routing API change and link it in the migration doc. Also add an internal eval to run 1 week before flip with smoke tests verifying per-route billing doesn't regress.

kevin: For messaging: Draft email + console modal that appears to org admins 7 days before default flips. Also add an in-console migration wizard that lists top services using legacy header and quick links to repo PR templates.

maria: OK next steps:
- eng-platform (jordan) creates routing API toggle ticket + smoke test plan.
- devex (kevin) drafts docs + console banners, PR to docs repo.
- sdk owners (samir) implement param + warning logs in Python/TS/Go, add CI test to ensure shim order in Go.
- I'll coordinate dates and ping legal to confirm billing messaging.

samir: I'll prototype the Go init-order fix today and push a small PR to the go-sdk repo.

jordan: I'll loop in routing infra and add the tenant toggle ticket: https://git.redwood/s/routing/tickets/7821

kevin: docs PR: https://git.redwood/s/docs/pulls/451 (WIP)

maria: Thanks all. I'll post an RFC summary in #all-hands and schedule a 30m sync this week for cross-team alignment.

kevin: :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks, will coordinate with oncall for the canary window.

release-bot: canary pipeline started for python-sdk@0.48.0-canary.1 and ts-sdk@1.12.0-canary.2

maria: If you hit edge cases while testing, drop replies here and tag me.

samir: noted, will report back with Go PR link later today.
